DTR · TALK ABOUT A SCENE

Spell It or Stay Locked

STS-HS12-L1-13001400-HSELA1112-ESC-EUR-01 • HS English 11-12 • Spell Correctly
Look at the picture. You will answer some questions about it. Press the play button to hear each question. Record your answer for each question. You can listen to your answer and record it again. Click SUBMIT RECORDINGS when you have answered all the questions.
JUST FOR FUN · OPTIONAL
Every lock in this room was built out of a spelling argument that Europe never finished. When printers in Mainz and Bruges and Westminster began setting English into metal type, they froze whichever spelling happened to be in the tray that day, and some of those choices were accidents. Printers who came from the Low Countries slid a silent h into the word ghost, and five hundred years later it is still sitting there. The last padlock on this wall opens for one word, and the room will not tell you which spelling of it is the real one.
Which English word do you think is spelled the most unfairly, and what would you change about it?
Optional. You do not have to record this one.
1
What is Ingrid doing?
Look at the picture. Name exactly what Ingrid is doing. Use the precise verb, not a general word like doing or it.
2
What is Tomasz holding?
Look at the picture. Name exactly what Tomasz is holding up. Use the precise noun, not a general word like thing or object.
3
What is the teacher doing?
Look at the picture. Name exactly what the teacher is doing. Use the precise verb, not a general word like working.
4
What place is this? How do you know?
Look at the picture. Name this place with the precise word, then name the clearest detail that shows it.
5
Tell me about the lock wall.
Look at the picture. Name three parts of the lock wall using precise nouns.
6
Tell me about what Mirela is wearing.
Look at the picture. Name the color and the exact garment Mirela is wearing, not a general word like clothes.
Record an answer for each question, then submit.
